# CAREX Folding Walker for Seniors, 30-37 Inches, 1 Count
Brand: Carex Health Brands
Category: Walkers, Rollators & Accessories > Standard Walkers

## Features
FOLDING WALKER. An adult walker that easily folds for transportation. Simply press on the two buttons and the walker folds up nicely. Walker is very sturdy, stable, and safe, made of 1 inch round aluminum construction. Supports a 300lb person.; HEIGHT ADJUSTABLE WALKER. A walker for seniors that is height adjustable. Marked peg holes allow the walker to be adjusted from 30-37 inches in height. Simply push the adjustment buttons in and slide the aluminum walker tubes up or down.No Backrest; LIGHTWEIGHT WALKER. The mobility walker is very light and maneuverable and has sides that detach for storing in tight spaces. Walker only weighs 6 pounds.; ADD WHEELS and make this walker a rolling walker with wheels. Wheel attachment sold separately. Wheels are perfect for the elderly, seniors, or handicap with problems lifting the weight of the walker. Walker glides can also be added to the bottom of this walker.; TRUST CAREX, a leader in walkers for seniors and walkers for elderly. Carex Health Brands has been the branded leader in rollators, walkers, and adult mobility walkers for over 35 years.

## Specifications
Product Dimensions: 3.5 x 20 x 18 inches; 6.6 Pounds; Date First Available: October 22, 2014

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 49.99 USD.
Rated 4.6 from 852 reviews.
Top review: Sturdy & strong. Helps me get around safely and independently. Helps getting up and down, can go up & down one step without help. Easy to put together, just a few pieces to snap together. Folds easily. Very light. Good price too. I thought I should mention a few things that make it easier for me to get around. I added wheels to the front and ski glides to the back. This was an inexpensive addition and helps me move a little faster while still maintaining balance. I talked about going up and down a step. This has been so helpful in maintaining my independence. Curbs obviously don’t have railings and I sometimes have to walk far to find a ramp. Steps sometimes don’t have a railing or often only have one which makes it difficult and unsafe when you are experiencing issues with pain, strength and/or balance. Now I can walk right up to the curb or step, put the walker up on the curb/step and climb up or put it down at ground level and step down and use the walker to support me like a railing. There are very helpful YouTube videos that helped me make sure I was doing this safely. I can also get in and out of my car by myself. I can push myself up onto the seat and use the steering wheel to help guide me into the car. The walker is so light that I can easily lift it in or out of the car by myself. I slide it in the car and place it upside down on the passenger side. It fits securely on the floor and I don’t have to worry about it sliding around and becoming dangerous or difficult for me to reach. Getting out is easier for me because my car is elevated a little bit and I can put the walker on the ground and lean on it to step down. I have used it in other people’s cars that are lower to the ground and I have needed help to pull myself up. I have also purchased a “door cane” that fits into the door latch and becomes a handle that gives you support to get in or out of the car. It is very helpful. This walker has also helped me in restrooms. In public restrooms one safety rail isn’t enough for me and most people don’t have a safety rail in their home bathroom. I found that carefully turning the walker around and pushing it all the way back against the toilet tank turns it into a safety rail. This allows me to safely sit and stand while holding on to the arms of the walker. I hope this helps someone, no matter which walker you choose. But I have had this walker for over a year now and it has remained strong and has allowed me to maintain my independence and safely navigate the challenges in my life.

Top review: Before my husband's knee surgery, I purchased both the typical aluminum walker for use around the house and the Carex Hemi walker for the bathroom. Both are important tools for different reasons. He uses the Carex Hemi walker in the bathroom and in the shower. It is smaller and lightweight and can be used for support on one side. He places the walker in front of him and uses the lower handle on the Hemi for support when getting up and down. It's also easy to move the Hemi inside the shower for stability. That said, he had to learn how to position his hands for balance so that he didn't fall to one side. When used properly and as intended, this walker is perfect.

Top review: This is about the third or fourth of these I have purchased--I get about a year out of them as I use it alot outside the home and strapped to the back of a motorcycle. I also remove the FRONT legs and replace with WHEELED legs from a standard walker--these hold up and I have been using the same ones over again and just painted to match. Takes 5 minutes to do this. Like that this comes in a COLOR and doesn't look so "Nursing home-ish" for me. I get a LOT of comments on it when we unpack it off the bike and have sent many people to buy one of their own. IT also is rumored to fold and fit in an airline overhead. The CLIPS that are supposed to hold the legs together when folded---don't--so use a bungie. It does stay folded in thirds when stashed in the car tho without a bungie either between the seats or in the trunk. Bungie is only needed when base of legs is also folded and needs to stay that way.
